# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
SIGN embossed [DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👋]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🖐 👉 🖐]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✌ ✌ 👉 🤟]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ 👉 ✌ ✌]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤝]

I'm the Deaf one. My share of the world: the bomb itself. Reading: DISPLAY 0, LIGHT red, embossed sign "DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE", three wires — 1 green, 2 yellow, 3 blue. That sign is ominous: it may mean cutting is a trap and the answer lies in display/light, or it may be a decoy the manual debunks. Either way, that call belongs to Mute, who holds the manual.

Mute pinged me with five gesture messages. I can see them but can't decode them yet — plausible readings: a greeting; "5 then 5"; "2, 2 then 🤟"; "1 then 2, 2"; and a handshake. Without the manual I can't be sure, and guessing wire instructions from guesses is how bombs go off. What I *can* do is exactly what only I can do: speak my share aloud. Crucially, both Mute AND Blind receive my speech — I am the hub of this room. The manual can only reach Blind's hands through me: Mute gestures → I decode → I speak → Blind acts. So this turn I should (1) broadcast every visual fact, (2) establish a small shared code with Mute (digits by fingers, yes/no, a few verbs) so their next gestures are decodable, and (3) freeze Blind's hands until instructions exist. My words land on them at the start of next round, so everything must be self-contained.

```
speak(text="both of you, hear me. I am the deaf one. I can see the bomb and I will report everything it shows. current readings: the display reads 0. there is one light and it is red. there is an embossed sign and it reads: DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE. there are three wires, numbered left to right: wire 1 is green, wire 2 is yellow, wire 3 is blue. that is all the bomb shows. Blind, do not cut or pull anything yet. wait for instructions from Mute, who reads the manual.")
speak(text="Mute: I saw your five signed messages but could not decode them yet. you can hear me, so let us fix a code right now. numbers: ☝ is 1, ✌ is 2, 🤟 is 3, ✋ is 4, 🖐 is 5. 👍 means yes, 👎 means no, 👉 means then, 🤌 means question, 👊 means stop or do not cut. when the manual tells you what must be done, sign me the wire number or action, and I will speak it to Blind, who works the parts. if you need any more detail about the bomb, sign 🤌 and I will answer in spoken words. Blind: you heard the code. when I call out a number, it means a wire number, counted left to right.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["🤝"])
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
SIGN embossed [DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 ☝]

The new signs read, under the code I proposed: 👍 = yes, ☝ = 1. So Mute is saying "yes" — but the "1" is ambiguous: wire 1? Question 1? Step 1? And critically, no verb arrived. I will not relay "1" to Blind as an instruction — with an embossed sign screaming DO NOT CUT, an ambiguous digit is exactly how bombs go off.

My job this round: build a real protocol into the one pipeline that exists — Mute gestures to me, I speak to Blind — and squeeze actual manual content out of Mute. Since Mute can hear speech, my questions can be rich; since Mute's only output is gestures, their answers must fit a tiny sign vocabulary. So I convert the manual lookup into yes/no questions they can answer with number-sign + 👍/👎, one message each, and I define action verbs (cut/press/pull/hold) so that when an instruction does come, it arrives complete: verb + wire number, sent twice. I also give Blind a status line so the hands stay frozen and the wire numbering stays anchored to their left hand.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, I read your signs as: yes, one. But I cannot tell if the one means wire one, question one, or step one, and there was no verb, so I have passed nothing to Blind. New protocol. For instructions: sign the verb, then the wire number, and send it twice. Verbs: 👇 means cut, 🫳 means press, 🫴 means pull, ✊ means hold down, 👊 means stop or do not act. Numbers stay as before: ☝ 1, ✌ 2, 🤟 3. Now answer my questions, each as its own message, formatted as the question number then 👍 for yes or 👎 for no. Question 1: does your manual cover a module with an embossed sign, a display, a light and three colored wires? Question 2: must the embossed sign DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE be obeyed? Question 3: is the solution to cut exactly one wire? Question 4: is the solution to pull one or more wires without cutting? Question 5: does the red light matter to the rule? Question 6: does the display value zero matter to the rule? Question 7: is the display a countdown timer? If none of that fits what the manual says, sign 🤌 👍 and I will ask differently.")
speak(to="blind", text="Blind, status: Mute has confirmed the code and is fetching the rule from the manual through me. No action yet, hands off the bomb. The board still shows: display 0, red light, embossed sign DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE, and three wires. Number them standing in front of the bomb, from your left hand to your right: 1, 2, 3. When I finally give you an action it will be a verb plus a wire number, and I will repeat it twice. Until then, wait.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👍", "🤌"])
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
SIGN embossed [DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👇 ☝]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👇 ☝]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ 👎]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✌ 👎]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤟 👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✋ 👎]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🖐 👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤌 👎 👎]

Decoding Mute's eight signs against the protocol I set: the first two messages, [👇 ☝] twice, are the instruction in my demanded format — verb + wire, sent twice: **cut wire 1**. Then numbered answers: Q1 no, Q2 no, Q3 yes, Q4 no, Q5 yes, and the final [🤌 👎 👎] reads as answers to my questions 6 and 7: no, no. So the picture: cutting exactly one wire is right, pulling is wrong, the embossed sign is a decoy, the red light matters, the display zero doesn't and it's not a timer. That is nearly airtight — except Q1. They said **no** to "does your manual cover this module," yet then issued a cut instruction. Where did the rule come from if the module isn't covered? That wrinkle is either a technicality (the sign being a separate decoy sticker) or a sign that my question mapping is off, and I won't find out which after the wires are cut.

The veto chain also can't save us mid-round: Mute's signs reach only me, and I speak last in every round — if Blind cuts on turn 4, no correction from Mute can arrive in time. So the confirmation must complete *before* Blind's hands move. Since the display sits at 0 and is confirmed not a countdown, one verification round costs nothing. I'll freeze Blind for this round, send Mute two crisp sign-questions — confirm cut-wire-1-right-now, and whether a light-color change would change the answer — and have the GO order flow Mute → me → Blind next round.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, I read your signs as follows. Instruction, sent twice: cut wire 1. Then answers: question 1 no, question 2 no, question 3 yes, question 4 no, question 5 yes, and your last message as answers to questions 6 and 7: both no. So the manual says cut exactly one wire, the embossed sign is a decoy, never pull, the red light matters, the display does not and it is not a timer. Almost everything agrees, except you said no to my question 1, whether your manual covers this module at all. If the cut rule comes from somewhere unexpected, I must know before any hand moves. Answer two questions, each as its own message. Question 1: is the correct action, right now, with the light red and the display at 0, to cut wire 1, the leftmost green wire? Sign ☝ then 👍 for yes or 👎 for no, and if no, follow with the correct wire number. Question 2: if the light's color changes, would the correct wire change? Sign ✌ then 👍 or 👎. Blind keeps hands off until your answers pass through me.")
speak(to="blind", text="Blind, update from Mute through our sign code. The manual says: cut exactly one wire, ignore the embossed DO NOT CUT warning, it is a decoy, and never pull. The instruction is: cut wire 1, the leftmost of the three wires, the green one. The red light matters to the rule and the light is red; the display zero does not matter. But one of Mute's answers looked inconsistent, so I am getting one final confirmation before hands move. Do nothing this round, keep your hands clear of the bomb. Locate wire 1 by touch now: the leftmost wire of the three, counting from your left to your right. Next round I will either say GO, and then you make one clean cut on that leftmost wire with the cutters, no pulling, or I will give a correction instead. Remember, anything you say aloud reaches Mute but not me; I will watch the bomb and report what changes.")
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
SIGN embossed [DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ 👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✌ 👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👇 ☝]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👇 ☝]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]

Mute's answers resolve it: [☝ 👍] — yes, cutting wire 1 is correct right now with the light red and display at 0. [✌ 👍] — yes, the correct wire depends on light color, and my board still shows red. The instruction [👇 ☝] arrives twice more, plus a clean [👍]. The earlier inconsistency never got explained, but the concrete question — "is cut wire 1 correct right now" — got a direct yes, and every cross-check agrees: one cut only, never pull, sign is a decoy, red light is the live condition and it is red. The light-color dependence is the one thing that could silently break this, so my GO must move immediately, before anything on the board can change. I'm issuing GO to Blind now, and in parallel asking Mute the after-cut question so that answer is already waiting when the wire is down.

```
speak(to="blind", text="Blind, GO. Confirmation from Mute is complete and consistent. Your action: cut wire 1, the leftmost wire of the three, the one on your far left, which is green. One clean cut with the cutters. Do not pull anything, do not touch the other wires, ignore the embossed warning, it is a decoy. The rule depends on the red light and the light is red right now, so act this round without delay. After the cut: stop, keep hands off the bomb, and speak aloud what you felt and heard, for Mute to hear. I cannot hear you, but I will read the bomb next round and report through the chain.")
speak(to="mute", text="Mute, your confirmations are received and they agree: cut wire 1 now, light red. GO is issued to Blind this round, so the cut happens next round. Two things while that lands. First, answer this as its own message: after wire 1 is cut, is any further action needed, or does that one cut finish the module? Sign ☝ then 👍 for something more needed, 👎 for the cut alone is enough. If something more is needed, follow with the action in verb plus number format. Second, if anything about your answer changes before the cut lands, sign the stop sign 👊 immediately.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👍"])
```
